common: the two contributions are carried and traded as one stock («Quod totum suprascriptum habere» ... «portasti», no. 437 (I, 430); «cum quo toto suprascripto habere», no. 400 (I, 392)), and profit, and whatever remains after a loss, are divided on the whole («Si vero aliquid inde remanserit sicut iactavimus ita participemus», no. 334 (I, 330)). Modal state common, share 100% of n=30 contracts (common 30/30); no variant at >=10%; contracts from stratum A 4, from release recitals 26; distinct parties named 53 (OCR name variants unified by hand; approximate). Alternative reading: several-accounts, where a recital speaks of shares (sortes) in a ship (nos. 18, 31, 191) or of profit «pro quantitate tue suprascripte pecunie» (no. 533 (II, 73)); the shares describe the stock's place in the cargo, not separate accounts within the arrangement, so common is kept. symmetric: the traveller takes half of the profit («capitanea salva. prode vero quod inde Dominus dederit per veram medielatem tecum dividere») and bears the loss of his own contribution («nichil inde pars parti inquirere debeat, Si vero aliquid inde remanserit sicut iactavimus ita participemus»), both no. 334 (I, 330). He takes half the gain on a stock to which he gave a third, so his exposure is not proportional, but it runs both ways. single-venture: one voyage, named outward and back with a named muda or by a date, with account due on return; often with a clause forbidding a change of voyage («ita quod aliud taxidium mutare non debeam», no. 191 (I, 191)). Rule: single-venture = one outbound venture ending with return by a named muda or date; fixed-term = a period (years, or muda and thence one year) with repeated trips allowed; open = no end set. Modal state single-venture, share 88% of n=26 contracts (single-venture 23/26; fixed-term 3/26); variant(s) at >=10%: fixed-term; contracts from stratum A 4, from release recitals 22; distinct parties named 45 (OCR name variants unified by hand; approximate). Fixed-term cases (variant): nos. 59 (two years), 141 (two years), 142 (one year, then on «si vestre in unum convenissent voluntates»). Further acts outside the frequency show an open clause and at-will extensions: no. 13 (I, 12), 1073, «Ista collegancia sil inter nos usque dum nostre in unum conveniunt volumpltates»; nos. 106 (I, 107) «usque dum nostre in unuin conveniunt voluntates» and 270 (I, 265) «usque dum nostre in unum convenerint. volunlates» extend a first term at will; no. 123 (I, 123) two years; no. 389 (I, 382) muda and one year. The edition therefore has open-ended bilateral contracts that the sample did not draw. Decision point: the convoy-bounded term (a modo usque per totam muduam ...) read as one venture, not as fixed-term.
